content.user_title: Apply Engineering Principles to Software Changes
content.value_statement: Software changes can repeat avoidable design, debugging, and verification mistakes. This skill gives coding assistants explicit engineering principles for making simpler, better-supported decisions.
actual_capabilities: Guide root-cause debugging through reproduction, instrumentation, and questioning assumptions shared by failed fixes.
Recommend domain data structures, boundary validation, and types that prevent invalid states.
Guide simplification by reducing unnecessary layers, duplicated decisions, and shared mutable state.
Structure API migrations around caller inventories, coordinated removal, and explicit verification boundaries.
Recommend observable behavior tests, direct output verification, and repeatable verification scripts.
Review retry and restart behavior using idempotency and state reconciliation principles.
limitations: Provides written guidance, not bundled executables, automated enforcement, or a standalone analysis engine.
Requires project context and tool access to implement changes or verify results.
References additional skills that are not included, including a benchmark checklist and TypeScript guidance.
Some reference files are brief; applying the principles still requires engineering judgment.

use_cases.title: Diagnose recurring failures
use_cases.description: Use reproduction and evidence to identify a shared faulty assumption after repeated fixes fail.

use_cases.title: Plan a coordinated API migration
use_cases.description: Inventory internal callers, define verification boundaries, and remove the legacy path when compatibility requirements permit.

use_cases.title: Review design and test quality
use_cases.description: Assess domain models, validation boundaries, reader load, and whether tests assert observable behavior.

prompt_templates.title: Beginner: Review a small change
prompt_templates.prompt: Review [change] using poteto-principles. Identify unnecessary complexity, unclear state, and missing verification. Explain your recommendations without editing files.
prompt_templates.scenario: Get focused feedback before implementing a small change.

prompt_templates.title: Intermediate: Diagnose a recurring bug
prompt_templates.prompt: Investigate [bug] and these failed fixes: [attempts]. Reproduce the failure, identify shared assumptions, and propose the smallest root-cause fix with a behavioral regression test.

prompt_templates.title: Advanced: Plan an API migration
prompt_templates.prompt: Plan migration from [old API] to [new API]. Inventory callers and compatibility requirements. Define reversible phases, verification boundaries, and conditions for removing the old API.
prompt_templates.scenario: Coordinate internal callers without creating permanent compatibility layers.

prompt_templates.title: Expert: Review retry and concurrency safety
prompt_templates.prompt: Review [workflow] for shared mutable state, retries, and partial failures. Propose isolation or serialization, reconciliation steps, and direct checks for repeated runs and interrupted execution.
prompt_templates.scenario: Evaluate the reliability of stateful processing or lifecycle operations.

output_examples.input: Two fixes changed retry timing, but the same workers still receive most of the load.
output: Shared assumption: retry timing causes the imbalance.
Next evidence: count work assignments per worker across repeated runs.
If the same workers dominate, inspect assignment rules before changing timing again.
Verify any correction with both per-worker distribution and end-to-end behavior.

output_examples.input: Review a task model with a completion flag and an optional completion date.
output: The model permits a completed task without a completion date.
Represent open and completed tasks as distinct variants, with a required date for the completed variant.
Parse external records at the boundary and test both accepted and rejected states.

output_examples.input: Our API refactor adds an adapter, but all callers are internal.
output: Confirm that no external users require compatibility.
Inventory internal callers and migrate them in verifiable units.
Remove the old API after caller migration and verify the new observable contract.
Use an adapter only when a specific transition requires it, with an explicit removal condition.

best_practices: Provide the relevant code, observed behavior, constraints, and verification commands before requesting recommendations.
Define compatibility requirements and approval boundaries before planning migrations or autonomous edits.
Keep reproduction steps, direct checks, and measurement evidence with each proposed change.
anti_patterns: Applying every principle mechanically without checking project constraints or existing invariants.
Removing validation before confirming that every external input is parsed at the correct boundary.
Treating compilation, mock call counts, or agent reports as proof of correct user-visible behavior.

faq.question: What is poteto-principles?
faq.answer: It is a written collection of engineering principles for design, implementation, debugging, refactoring, migration, verification, and documentation work.

faq.question: Can I use it with Claude, Codex, and Claude Code?
faq.answer: The marketplace metadata lists all three tools. Actual file access, editing, and verification depend on the capabilities and permissions of your environment.

faq.question: Does the skill include scripts or an automated checker?
faq.answer: No. It contains Markdown guidance that recommends creating repeatable tools and checks when appropriate.

faq.question: Is the guidance specific to TypeScript?
faq.answer: No. Most principles are language-independent. The type-system reference includes examples from several languages and points to a separate TypeScript skill.

faq.question: Does it allow irreversible actions without approval?
faq.answer: No. Its autonomy guidance explicitly requires confirmation for force-pushing, deleting production data, and sending external messages.

faq.question: Does it include the linked benchmark checklist?
faq.answer: No. The measurement guidance links to a separate benchmark checklist that is not bundled with this skill.
